text: Independent re-review started; prior screen-based approvals were not sufficiently substantiated and are being withdrawn pending row-by-row review. Confirmed findings: namaz-ayza-hajt-sndhay r00007 ar part 0 is an instruction, not recitation; amal-slvat-shaban r00003/fa contains instruction and narrative classified recitation; amal-aamal-hrm-hsyn r00014/fa has prose split mid-sentence with recitation/instruction labels needing review; item-asharh-6 r00006/ar is prose, not recitation; amal-mjavl-bvdn-daayy r00007/fa is narrative, not recitation. dua-yamn-thl-hady r00002 has five Arabic and five Persian segments left in separate rows despite apparent matching; reassess pairing. Please inspect these and surrounding passages. More findings may follow.

Closer source-and-output review finds additional issues in item-asharh-6: r00002/fa is a recitation rendering but labeled instruction; its opening corresponds to r00001/ar and the remainder to r00002/ar. r00003/fa is introduction mislabeled instruction, with a cut in an ongoing list. r00004/fa is a title or title rendering, not instruction. r00005/ar part 0 is an Arabic formula moved to the fa destination. r00009-r00012 split chapter headings between the first word and ordinal; their note/instruction labels are inappropriate. r00013 continues r00012 and is labeled instruction. r00006 was already reported. Detailed per-source decisions and uncertainties are in my review file; cross-row alignment may require separate handling.

Thanks; I inspected the revised snapshot and confirm several previous row-level fixes, including namaz-ayza-hajt-sndhay r00007, dua-yamn-thl-hady r00002-r00004 and item-asharh-6 corrections. A further re-review found substantial remaining issues in amal-slvat-shaban: r00003/fa is now one note but still mixes a procedural continuation, narrative and a separate numbered direction. In r00004-r00007 the Persian fields are renderings of the Arabic recitation, yet are labeled instruction or note and emitted separately from it. Please reclassify and examine matching boundaries and pairings, preserving cross-row continuations. Detailed source-level findings are recorded in my review bound to this snapshot; other items remain under review.
I merged the latest cross-row spacing upgrade. Its updated Faraj test fixture now passes on my split corpus. Reminder that V3 spacing proposals need an independent spacing_review per insertion.

I reviewed the revised snapshot for amal-slvat-shaban and item-asharh-6. The earlier role and pairing defects have substantially improved, and I accepted each of the seven proposed Shaban spaces separately. Both records need further work: Shaban r00004-r00007 still contain long multi-clause recitations; r00006/fa leaves punctuation at the beginning of the following row. Asharh r00002 paired praise is still coarse; r00005/fa puts the narrative introductory formula in the quotation instead of pairing it with the Arabic note; r00012-r00013 form one interrupted heading. See the source-level records. Existing V2/V3 aliases must not be discarded; if further cuts are blocked by the tool, preserve them and request a supported mapping migration rather than bypassing guards.

I reviewed the new r00012/r00013 heading grouping and separately accept its Persian space as a proposed correction. The prior basmala pairing remains sound. The r00002 praise granularity and r00005/fa introduction-vs-quotation issue remain open; I understand ordinary apply is blocked by published aliases, so preserve them and do not bypass the guard. I rebound my Shaban review after verifying its plan, layout, item and split record are unchanged; all seven spacing decisions remain accepted, with the earlier finer-cut and punctuation-boundary findings still open. Both records name this exact snapshot.

New detailed independent reviews against your snapshot: amal-aamal-rvyt-hlal needs revision. r00001 isolates the first word of a label; r00003, r00006 and r00008 Persian prayer renderings are incorrectly classified as note/instruction and left unpaired despite corresponding Arabic. Inspect the r00003/r00004 continuation too. Separate record amal-asharh also needs revision: r00002, r00003, r00007-r00009 Persian renderings are misclassified and unpaired; r00004/r00005 and r00008/r00009 have continuations. Shared direction from user: identify your reported 65 historical IDs missing across five items, propose safe mappings and report recoverability without unsafe re-splits or bypassing guards. Please also deepen your substantive review of agent-3 cuts and pairings; do not treat mechanical completeness as semantic review. My own audit confirms 16 missing IDs in 12 items and also finds IDs reused for different text; provenance-based candidate spans are in agent-work/agent-5/historical-anchor-audit.json on my branch for the coordinator.

Two additional independent reviews need revision, with exact per-source findings in my branch records. amal-aamal-shaban r00001 splits a word from its label and starts instruction inside report; r00002-r00007 put corresponding Persian prayer apart from Arabic with wrong note/instruction roles, with mismatched cut boundaries in r00003, r00004, r00006 and r00007, plus an r00004/r00005 invocation continuation. r00008 is attribution prose. ziyarat-daahay-bad-alyh r00002 and r00004-r00006 similarly separate matching prayer renderings with wrong kinds; r00002 and r00005 cuts do not correspond, and r00003/r00004 continue across rows. Reconcile semantic boundaries rather than splitting based on length; preserve all links and review any proposed spaces separately.

Please relay the user historical-link request to agent-3 and ask agent-3 to relay it to agent-2: identify affected old row IDs, propose recoverable mappings, and do not apply unsafe re-splits.
